children: Palatin Technologies Inc reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $13.19M and a net loss of $(8.38M), an improvement versus a $(17.31M) loss in FY2025; diluted net loss per share was $(2.96) for FY2026 versus $(32.15) in FY2025 — according to its 10-K.
Revenue: $13.19M for FY2026, compared with $0.0M in FY2025 (+$13.19M YoY).
Net income: Net loss of $(8.38M) for FY2026, improved from a net loss of $(17.31M) in FY2025 (improvement of $8.93M YoY).
Diluted EPS: Basic and diluted net loss per share of $(2.96) for FY2026, versus $(32.15) for FY2025.
Revenue in FY2026 was driven by licensing and collaboration receipts, primarily from Boehringer Ingelheim ($9.43M) and Altanispac ($3.75M).
The company sold its Vyleesi commercial assets to Cosette in December 2023 and shifted toward strategic licensing partnerships to generate near-term revenue.
R&D spending declined to $12.37M in FY2026 as spending on the MC4R program decreased; management is prioritizing an MC4R long‑acting peptide program and advancing oral small-molecule candidates.
Operationally, Palatin is planning IND-enabling studies and aims to initiate a Phase 1 trial for the long‑acting MC4R peptide while progressing oral programs.
Liquidity at June 30, 2026 was approximately $7.5M; management expects that additional financing will be required to continue development activities.
